title: The King's Dominion
summary: When Francisco's enemies launch a coordinated assault that destroys the Resource Web, scatters his community, and undermines his fourth-path strategy, he faces the King of Disks' trial: building empire not through conquest but through sustainable influence that survives catastrophe. In the wasteland of apparent defeat, Francisco discovers that his true power lies not in his temporal abilities or strategic brilliance but in his capacity to inspire others to hope and action despite overwhelming odds. Through two crucial movements, he learns that empire-building means creating systems and inspiring people who can sustain purpose without his constant presence. The King of Disks represents mastery of material reality and practical wisdom—leadership that builds lasting structures rather than dependent followers. Francisco transforms from individual hero to empire-builder who multiplies impact through ethical authority and strategic vision that empowers collective resilience.

scenes.setup: Days after Francisco's visionary expansion, his enemies strike with devastating coordination. The attack isn't direct confrontation—it's systematic dismantling. The Resource Web collapses as key nodes are corrupted. The fourth-path allies scatter, convinced Francisco led them to disaster. The Diplomatic Circle publicly denounces him for disrupting established order. Worst of all: timeline refugees he swore to protect are captured, their fates uncertain. Francisco stands in the ruins of the Hall of Deliberation, surrounded by destruction and abandoned by those he served. The King of Disks appears not in glory but sitting on rubble—showing that true kingship is tested in devastation, not triumph. Zara remains, but even her presence feels like burden rather than support. Francisco must choose: retreat into bitterness and self-protection, or find a way to build empire from ruins by inspiring revival in broken hearts.
scenes.symbolism: The ruins represent how success creates vulnerability—enemies studied Francisco's systems and struck at foundations. The King on rubble shows that sovereignty means responsibility for reconstruction, not just celebration of achievement. Scattered allies demonstrate that dependent followers abandon leaders in crisis—empire requires autonomous commitment. Timeline refugees' capture reveals the cost of leadership: others suffer for his choices.
scenes.beat_goal: Establish the all-is-lost devastation: systematic destruction testing whether Francisco builds empire through dependency or sustainable inspiration
scenes.scene_tone: Bleak and catastrophic with underlying resilience question
scenes.location: Ruins of the Hall of Deliberation - Destruction Field

scenes.setup: Francisco begins not with grand strategy but with single action: he sits among the rubble and starts rebuilding with his own hands. One by one, people emerge from hiding to watch. He doesn't command or inspire with words—he demonstrates that purpose survives catastrophe through persistent action. Slowly, others join: first Zara, then students, then former allies who thought all was lost. Francisco teaches as he builds: empire isn't structures but systems of shared commitment that survive individual failure. He reveals the King of Disks' wisdom: true sovereignty means building people's capacity to sustain purpose without his constant direction. They don't just rebuild the Hall—they create distributed nodes so no single strike can destroy their network again. As refugees are rescued through coordinated effort, Francisco realizes his role has evolved: not hero solving problems but king building sustainable systems and inspiring autonomous commitment. The empire he builds isn't territory but network of people empowered to lead themselves, united by shared purpose rather than dependent on his presence.
scenes.symbolism: Francisco building with his own hands represents servant leadership—sovereignty through service not command. People emerging from hiding shows how hope spreads through demonstrated commitment rather than inspiring speeches. Distributed nodes symbolize empire built on resilience—decentralized strength survives centralized attacks. Rescued refugees represent collective power—empire means coordinated autonomous action, not individual heroism.
scenes.beat_goal: Demonstrate empire-building through sustainable influence: inspiring autonomous commitment that survives catastrophe and leader absence
scenes.core_emotion: Awe at transformation from devastation to collective power
scenes.scene_tone: Rising and empowering with hard-won wisdom
scenes.location: Ruins Transforming to Distributed Network - Revival Field
